subject: Communication
title: Authority: Why We Obey Experts
description: Learn Authority: Why We Obey Experts in one minute.

hook.text: A man in a lab coat tells you to shock a stranger. Most people comply. That was Milgram's experiment.

buildup.text: Stanley Milgram found that 65% of participants delivered maximum 'shocks' when an authority figure insisted.

discovery.text: We obey authority figures because it's usually efficient — doctors, pilots, experts generally know best.

twist.text: But authority cues are easy to fake. A white coat, a title, or a confident tone triggers obedience.

climax.text: Advertisers use 'doctors recommend' because the authority shortcut bypasses critical thinking entirely.

punchline.text: We follow authority on autopilot. That's the feature and the bug.

quiz.question: What did Milgram's experiment demonstrate about authority?
options: Most people obey authority figures even against their conscience

details.summary: We defer to perceived authorities, whether doctors, professors, or uniformed officials, even when their expertise is irrelevant. Milgram's experiments showed that ordinary people will follow authority to shocking extremes. Titles, uniforms, and confidence all trigger this response.
details.whyItMatters: Authority shortcuts save time in complex decisions but can be exploited. Questioning credentials and relevance is essential critical thinking.
takeaways: People obey authority figures even against their judgment
Symbols of authority like titles and uniforms trigger compliance

faq.question: What did Milgram's obedience experiments actually show?
faq.answer: Participants administered what they believed were dangerous electric shocks to others simply because an experimenter in a lab coat told them to continue. About 65 percent obeyed to the maximum voltage. The study revealed how easily authority overrides personal morality.

faq.question: How can you tell if an authority is legitimate?
faq.answer: Ask whether their expertise is relevant to the specific claim. A Nobel physicist has no special authority on nutrition. Check for conflicts of interest, verify credentials independently, and remember that genuine experts welcome questions rather than demanding blind trust.
